headline.caveat: full syndicate facility with Goldman Sachs Bank USA as identifiable lead; also JPMorgan Chase Bank, Mizuho Securities USA, Apollo Global Funding, and SMBC

realized_to_date.caveat: signed early Aug 2026; SoftBank planned to draw within the month — drawdown not yet confirmed as of Aug 13, 2026

nature_md: SoftBank secured a $10B, two-year margin loan (one-year extension option) **collateralized by its OpenAI stake** — its ~$64.6B planned OpenAI position pledged against bank debt. Priced at ~SOFR+425bp (~7.9% at signing), nearly triple the spread of SoftBank's 2018 Alibaba margin loan, reflecting private (unlisted) collateral. Lenders: Goldman Sachs Bank USA, JPMorgan Chase Bank NA, Mizuho Securities USA, Apollo Global Funding, and Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. Proceeds fund general corporate purposes and Vision Fund II-2. Provisions require additional collateral or early repayment if OpenAI's preferred shares suffer a sharp valuation decline — a direct transmission channel from OpenAI's private mark to SoftBank's liquidity. Stacks on top of the separate $40B unsecured bridge (see related edge).

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Secured lending on the syndicate banks' books against unlisted preferred shares — collateral that cannot be sold quickly and whose 'price' is a funding-round mark. The margin-call mechanics make the banks' protection procyclical: it tightens exactly when OpenAI's valuation weakens.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Non-recourse-style leverage against SoftBank's largest asset without selling it: debt on SoftBank's balance sheet, collateral pledged. SoftBank has now sold its entire NVIDIA stake, borrowed $40B unsecured, and margined its OpenAI stake to keep funding its AI program — a leverage stack senior official-sector observers cite in the credit-cycle debate.

both_sides_md: **Bear:** borrowing at ~7.9% against an illiquid private mark, with collateral-top-up triggers, is late-cycle leverage — if OpenAI's valuation resets, SoftBank faces margin calls on a stake it cannot sell (Bloomberg's spread comparison vs the Alibaba loan makes the risk repricing explicit). **Bull:** the loan is small against the stake's ~$64.6B planned cost basis (let alone its mark), monetizes an appreciated asset without dilution ahead of a potential OpenAI IPO, and five top-tier lenders accepting OpenAI paper as collateral is itself institutional validation of the asset class.

events.title: SoftBank signs $10B margin loan backed by OpenAI stake at ~SOFR+425bp
